response.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean FROM per_rating) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_ratio AS avg_rate_per_day, p.avg_ratio - o.overall_mean AS diff_above_overall_mean FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE o.overall_mean IS NOT NULL AND p.avg_ratio > o.overall_mean ORDER BY p.rating

assumptions.assumption: The ratio rental_rate / rental_duration is computed per film (rental_duration is verified as 3-7, so there is no division by zero). Each rating is averaged over its qualifying films. The overall mean is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages, not a film-level average.

The ratings with at least one film at replacement_cost >= 20.99 are grouped as stored, and a NULL rating (if one existed) would count as its own group. The verified data shows exactly 5 rating levels.
